topicName: Bitwise Operators: AND, OR, XOR, NOT, Shift Operators
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Bitwise Operators in Data Structures & Algorithms"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Bitwise operators perform operations on individual bits of data. They are fundamental in low-level programming, data manipulation, and algorithm optimization. Understanding these operators is crucial for efficient memory usage and performance."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"AND Operator (&)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The AND operator (&) performs a bitwise AND operation. The result is 1 only if both corresponding bits are 1; otherwise, the result is 0."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"Example (in C++):
int a = 5;  // Binary: 0101
int b = 3;  // Binary: 0011
int result = a & b; // Binary: 0001, Decimal: 1"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"OR Operator (|)"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"The OR operator (|) performs a bitwise OR operation. The result is 1 if at least one of the corresponding bits is 1; otherwise, the result is 0."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"Example (in C++):
int a = 5;  // Binary: 0101
int b = 3;  // Binary: 0011
int result = a | b; // Binary: 0111, Decimal: 7"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"XOR Operator (^)"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"The XOR operator (^) performs a bitwise exclusive OR operation. The result is 1 if the corresponding bits are different; otherwise, the result is 0."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"Example (in C++):
int a = 5;  // Binary: 0101
int b = 3;  // Binary: 0011
int result = a ^ b; // Binary: 0110, Decimal: 6"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"NOT Operator (~)"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"The NOT operator (~) performs a bitwise NOT operation. It inverts each bit: 0 becomes 1, and 1 becomes 0.  Note that the result is often dependent on the system's integer representation (e.g., two's complement)."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"Example (in C++):
int a = 5;  // Binary: 0101
int result = ~a; // Binary: 1010 (depending on the system, this will be a negative number)"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Left Shift Operator (<<)"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"The left shift operator (<<) shifts the bits of a number to the left by a specified number of positions. Vacant positions are filled with zeros.  This is equivalent to multiplying the number by 2 raised to the power of the shift amount."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"Example (in C++):
int a = 5;  // Binary: 0101
int result = a << 2; // Binary: 010100, Decimal: 20 (5 * 2^2)"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Right Shift Operator (>>)"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"The right shift operator (>>) shifts the bits of a number to the right by a specified number of positions. The behavior of filling the vacant positions depends on whether it's a logical or arithmetic shift.  For positive numbers, it's generally equivalent to dividing the number by 2 raised to the power of the shift amount."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"Example (in C++):
int a = 20; // Binary: 00010100
int result = a >> 2; // Binary: 00000101, Decimal: 5 (20 / 2^2)"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Note: The behavior of the right shift operator on negative numbers can be implementation-dependent. Some implementations perform an arithmetic shift (sign extension), while others perform a logical shift (fill with zeros)."},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Applications"},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Setting, clearing, and toggling specific bits in a data structure."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Implementing efficient set operations (union, intersection, difference) using bitsets."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Performing fast multiplication and division by powers of 2 using shift operators."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cryptography and hashing algorithms."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Image processing and data compression."}]
